review_target: server/migrations/004_access_control.up.sql — hostile security review of the implemented migration, against user-spec.md, tech-spec.md (Decisions 3/4/5, Data Models, Risks table) and tasks/1.md. Verified empirically against a live mariadb:11.4 container (docker compose db service) with migrations 001-004 applied, not just read statically.
summary: The file is a verbatim, byte-for-byte match of the tech-spec's Data Models SQL block. No SQL injection surface exists (static file, zero interpolation, zero external input at migration time) — confirmed by inspection. Idempotency holds under adversarial re-run: verified live by re-executing the full file a second time directly via mariadb client (bypassing migrate.go's version-skip) — no error, admin count stayed at exactly 2. It also holds under partial-failure retry because every operator is independently idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS / ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE) and MariaDB DDL auto-commits per-statement, so a crash between any two statements in the batch leaves a state that a full re-run repairs without duplication. The CHECK-constraint-lets-NULL-through concern the design review raised (test-reviewer-design-1.json) does not materialize in the deployed schema: both role and status are NOT NULL, verified live — NULL insertion fails with error 1048 before CHECK is ever evaluated, and an out-of-enum value fails with 4025 (chk_users_role / chk_access_requests_status both enforce correctly). The hardcoded-admin-logins trade-off itself is sound and consistent with what Decision 4 and the Risks table already accept: the placeholder that a prior tech-spec security review round flagged as high-severity (ADMIN_LOGIN_2) is gone — both logins are real, and the rationale for hardcoding (auto-applied, irreversible, no down-migrations, editing after-the-fact doesn't retract seeded rows) is now accurately reflected in this file's comments-equivalent tech-spec prose, so that acceptance still holds and is not re-flagged as new. One finding from that same tech-spec security review round was NOT addressed by this migration and I reproduced it live: users.id has no explicit COLLATE, inherits the database default utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci (case- AND accent-insensitive, confirmed via information_schema and SHOW CREATE TABLE), and I confirmed empirically that inserting login 'rogogdbd' collides with the seeded 'RoGogDBD' row rather than creating a second one. This happens to be the benign direction for these two specific logins (no self-bricking, no silent second admin-less row) but it means the authorization key for role='admin' is not an exact-match key — identity resolution rides on a global server collation setting rather than an explicit, migration-declared one. This is a real, still-open gap, not a new one I'm inventing.

findings.owasp: A02:2021 - Cryptographic Failures / A04:2021 - Insecure Design (identity key relies on ambient collation, not an explicit one)
findings.location: server/migrations/004_access_control.up.sql:1-6 (users.role, chk_users_role) and the pre-existing server/migrations/002_costing_schema.up.sql:1-4 (users.id VARCHAR(255), no explicit COLLATE) that this migration's seed INSERT (lines 27-30) writes into
findings.description: Verified live against the actual docker-compose db (mariadb:11.4.12, database default collation utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci — confirmed via `SELECT DEFAULT_COLLATION_NAME FROM information_schema.SCHEMATA` and `SHOW FULL COLUMNS FROM users`): `id` is case- and accent-insensitive. Reproduced the consequence directly: `INSERT INTO users (id, role, has_access) VALUES ('rogogdbd','user',FALSE) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE role=role` did not create a second row — it collided with the seeded 'RoGogDBD' row and left it untouched, because MariaDB treats the two strings as equal under this collation. This is the same gap the tech-spec's own round-2 security review flagged (work/access-control/logs/techspec/security-review.json, medium finding at 'tech-spec.md — Data Models (seed uses RoGogDBD)... users.id VARCHAR(255), default collation'), and grep across the current, approved tech-spec.md shows no COLLATE/normalization decision was ever added to close it — Decision 11 (EnsureUser) still has no lowercasing/trimming step, and this migration still declares no explicit COLLATE on users.id or in the seed INSERT. For the two current logins the collision direction happens to be safe (mixed-case 'RoGogDBD' and the real Yandex-returned login collapse to the same row, so the admin doesn't get bricked into a second powerless row — the failure mode the round-2 review worried about most). But the underlying design smell is real and this migration is the artifact that bakes the two literal login strings in: nothing here declares that users.id is meant to be an exact-match security key, and role resolution for 'is this caller an admin' now depends on a database-server default that is not asserted anywhere in schema or tests. If the server's default collation setting ever changes (config drift, image upgrade, a future migration on a differently-provisioned environment), the two admin rows and any real login attempting to match them could silently diverge into separate rows with different roles.
findings.recommendation: Not a blocker for this task specifically (it inherits from migration 002 and a design decision the tech-spec explicitly left open), but worth flagging up to the tech-spec/task-decomposition level rather than closing silently: either declare `id VARCHAR(255) COLLATE utf8mb4_bin` explicitly (paired with explicit lowercase/trim normalization of the login everywhere it's compared: EnsureUser, RequireAdmin, the admin {login} path segment, and this seed INSERT) so the key is exact-match and self-documenting, or explicitly accept case/accent-insensitive identity as a documented, permanent property of the login key with a one-line acceptance note next to Decision 4 — right now it is neither declared nor tested, just inherited from server defaults.

findings.description: Re-checked whether hardcoding two admin logins in a committed, auto-applied, irreversible SQL file is acceptable given this specific project's constraints, rather than treating it as a fresh finding. It is. Three things independently support the tech-spec's acceptance: (1) migrations.Run() in server/cmd/main.go:32-34 runs unconditionally on every container start and log.Fatalf's on error, so a malformed file is a deploy-blocking crash-loop, not a silent partial apply — verified this is the actual wiring, not a spec claim; (2) migrate.go records applied versions in schema_migrations and skips them thereafter (verified in migrate.go:32-36), so a hand-edit to this file after any environment has run it is genuinely inert there, exactly as the tech-spec states — meaning a plaintext placeholder would have been a real, unfixable-by-file-edit problem, but the file as written contains no placeholder ('ADMIN_LOGIN_2' from the earlier tech-spec review round is gone, replaced by the real 'RoGogDBD' and 'irina2000aleshina'); (3) the ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE construction (not UPDATE) is the correct idempotent-and-createable primitive given point (2) — verified live that a second raw run leaves exactly 2 admin rows. Given no down-migrations exist anywhere in this project (confirmed: only *.up.sql files present, migrate.go has no down-path) and the operational alternative (ADMIN_LOGINS env var) was already explicitly rejected upstream by the user per Decision 4's Alternatives Considered, hardcoding real, final login values in this specific file is the least-bad mechanism available and matches what actually ships. No action needed here.
findings.recommendation: None — recorded as verified-still-holds, not a new finding. The one adjacent gap (collation/identity-key exactness) is filed separately above since it's a different, still-open concern the round-2 review also raised and the tech-spec did not resolve.

findings.description: Checked for SQL injection surface as requested. None exists: this is a static, hand-authored file with zero string interpolation, zero placeholders substituted at build/deploy time, and zero external input reaching it — migrate.go (line 43) reads the file's bytes verbatim via embed.FS and passes them to db.Exec() unchanged. The two seeded login literals ('RoGogDBD', 'irina2000aleshina') are fixed values, not derived from any request, config var, or template substitution. There is no vector here for an attacker to influence the SQL text.
findings.recommendation: None — confirms the task's own framing that no injection surface should exist here.

findings.owasp: A04:2021 - Insecure Design (verification only, CHECK/NULL question from design review)
findings.description: The design review (test-reviewer-design-1.json) raised, as a hypothetical regression risk, that CHECK (role IN (...)) does not reject NULL under standard SQL semantics (NULL IN (...) is UNKNOWN, which CHECK treats as satisfied). Verified this is correctly moot in the migration as actually written: `role VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user'` and `status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'` are both NOT NULL, so NULL can never reach the CHECK evaluation at all. Confirmed live: `INSERT INTO users (id, role) VALUES ('x', NULL)` fails with error 1048 ('Column role cannot be null') before any CHECK logic runs; a genuinely out-of-enum value ('superadmin') correctly fails with 4025 (constraint chk_users_role). Same pattern confirmed for chk_access_requests_status. The design review's finding was a legitimate regression-detection gap for the test suite (a future hand-edit that drops NOT NULL wouldn't be caught by a presence-only column check) — that is a testing-coverage concern, correctly scoped to the test-reviewer, not a live vulnerability in this file today.
findings.recommendation: None for this file. The test-coverage angle (assert full column definition including Null=NO, not just presence) belongs to the test-reviewer's report for this task, not this security review.
